title: Writing a laboratory report
competency: Write a clear laboratory report with its parts in the right order.

keywords.def: A place where science experiments are done. It builds observation skills, skill with apparatus and independent thinking.
A written account of the results of an experiment, written precisely and clearly.
What you want to find out or show in an experiment.
The steps you followed, in order.
What you saw and measured while you worked.
A short answer to your objective.

en.text: The laboratory is where science experiments are done. It builds your observation, your skill with apparatus and your independent thinking. A laboratory report is a written account of the results of an experiment. Write it precisely and clearly, with good grammar and punctuation.

am.text: ቤተ ሙከራ የሳይንስ ሙከራዎች የሚደረጉበት ቦታ ነው። የቤተ ሙከራ ሪፖርት የሙከራ ውጤቶች የጽሑፍ መግለጫ ነው። በትክክል፣ በግልጽ እና በጥሩ ሰዋስው መጻፍ አለበት።

screens.title: A friend was absent
screens.text: Your class in Bahir Dar tested which cloth dries fastest. Your friend Liya was absent that day.
screens.ask: What is the best way for Liya to learn what you did and found?
opts: Read a clear written report of the experiment
screens.after:
Liya was not there to see the test.
A clear written report tells her what you did, saw and found.
Guessing or looking at empty beakers tells her nothing.
Scientists write reports for this reason. Read on.
screens.best: Read a clear written report of the experiment

screens.title: 1.2.4 Writing a laboratory report
paras: The laboratory is the place where science experiments are done.
It builds your power of observation and skill with apparatus. It also builds independent thinking.

screens.title: What lab work builds
screens.ask: Tap each card to see what the laboratory builds in you.
items: You learn to watch closely and notice small changes.
You learn to use tools like the balance and the microscope.
You plan, test and decide for yourself.

screens.caption: A lab report tells what you did and found.

screens.title: What a report must be
paras: A laboratory report is a written account of the results of an experiment.
It should be written precisely and clearly, with good grammar and punctuation.

screens.title: The lab and the report
defs: The place where science experiments are done.
A written account of the results of an experiment, written precisely and clearly.

screens.title: What is a report?
opts: A teacher's marks for the class
A written account of the results of an experiment, written clearly
screens.ans: A written account of the results of an experiment, written clearly
screens.why:
Step 1: the book says a lab report is a written account of an experiment's results.
Step 2: it must be written precisely and clearly.
Step 3: it explains what you did, what you learnt and what the results mean.
So the answer is the last option.
A list of rules or a drawing alone is not a report.
screens.clue: Read the first sentence of "What a report must be".

screens.title: Finish the definition
screens.ask: Definition: a laboratory report is a written account of the ___ of an experiment.
screens.why:
An experiment ends with results.
A lab report is a written account of those results.
So the missing word is results.
screens.clue: What does an experiment give you at the end?

screens.title: Fix the report
screens.text: Kebede wrote his report in a hurry. It has no full stops and many unclear words.
opts: Nothing, results are all that matter
Write it precisely and clearly, with good grammar and punctuation
Make it longer with more pictures
screens.ans: Write it precisely and clearly, with good grammar and punctuation
screens.why:
Step 1: Kebede's report has no full stops and unclear words.
Step 2: the book says a report must be precise and clear.
Step 3: it also needs good grammar and punctuation.
So he should rewrite it precisely and clearly.
Copying a friend breaks honesty; more pictures do not fix unclear words.
screens.clue: How does the book say a report should be written?

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: What lab work builds: lab work helps students build independent thinking.
screens.why:
The book says lab work builds three things.
1: power of observation.
2: skill with apparatus.
3: independent thinking.
Independent thinking is in the list, so the statement is true.
screens.clue: Read the first paragraph of 1.2.4. What three things does the lab build?
screens.worked:
Step 1: the book lists what the lab builds.
Step 2: power of observation, skill with apparatus and independent thinking.
Step 3: independent thinking is in the list.
So the statement is true.

ideas.name: Parts of a laboratory report, in order

en.text: Every report has the same parts, in order. Date, title, objective, theory, materials, chemicals, procedure, observation, result, discussion, conclusion. First you say what you planned. Then what you did and saw. Last, what it means.

am.text: እያንዳንዱ ሪፖርት በቅደም ተከተል ተመሳሳይ ክፍሎች አሉት። ቀን፣ ርዕስ፣ ዓላማ፣ ንድፈ ሐሳብ፣ ቁሳቁሶች፣ ኬሚካሎች፣ የአሠራር ቅደም ተከተል፣ ምልከታ፣ ውጤት፣ ውይይት፣ መደምደሚያ።

screens.title: What comes first?
screens.text: You are about to write your first lab report.
screens.ask: Which part do you think comes first?
screens.after:
A report starts with when you did the experiment: the date.
Then comes the title, then the objective.
Observation, result and conclusion come later, after you do the work.
Read the list of parts to check.

screens.title: The parts of a report
screens.ask: Every report has these parts, in this order. Tap each part.
items: The day you did the experiment.
A short name for the experiment.
What you want to find out or show.
The science ideas behind the experiment.
The apparatus and equipment you used.
The steps you followed, in order.
What you saw and measured while you worked.
The outcome of the experiment, such as a table of readings.
What the results mean and why they came out that way.
A short answer to your objective.

screens.title: Key parts
defs: What you want to find out or show.
The steps you followed, in order.
What you saw and measured while you worked.
A short answer to your objective.

screens.title: A sample report: which cloth dries fastest?
steps: Date: the day you did the test.
Objective: to find which of three cloths dries fastest in the sun.
Materials: three cloths of the same size, a bucket of water, a clock.
Procedure: wet each cloth, squeeze it, hang all three in the sun, check every 10 minutes.
Observation and result: write the time each cloth became dry, in a table.
Conclusion: name the cloth that dried first. That answers the objective.

screens.title: Where do readings go?
screens.ask: In which part of a report do you write what you saw and measured?
screens.why:
Step 1: what you saw and measured happens while you work.
Step 2: the part for that is the observation.
Step 3: the objective is what you want to find; the theory is the science behind it.
So the answer is observation.
screens.clue: Look at the "What it holds" column of the table.

screens.title: Put the parts in order
screens.text: Put these parts of a laboratory report in order.
screens.why:
Step 1: start with when and what: Date, then Title.
Step 2: then the plan: Objective, then Materials.
Step 3: then what you did and saw: Procedure, then Observation.
Step 4: then the outcome: Result.
Step 5: end with your answer: Conclusion.
screens.clue: Start with when and what. End with your answer to the objective.
screens.worked:
Date → Title → Objective → Materials → Procedure → Observation → Result → Conclusion.
Plan first, then do and see, then decide.

screens.title: The last part
screens.ask: Parts of a report: the part that gives a short answer to your objective is the ___.
screens.why:
The objective asks what you want to find out.
At the end you answer it in a few words.
That last part is the conclusion.
So the answer is conclusion.
screens.clue: It is the last of the eleven parts.

screens.title: Liya's list
screens.text: Liya writes: "beaker, thermometer, Bunsen burner, tongs".
screens.ask: Which part of her report is this?
screens.why:
Step 1: Liya's list is beaker, thermometer, Bunsen burner, tongs.
Step 2: these are all apparatus and equipment.
Step 3: the part that lists apparatus is materials.
So the answer is materials.
The objective would say what she wants to find out, not list tools.
screens.clue: Which part lists apparatus and equipment?

items.ask: 1. Which one is NOT allowed in a science laboratory?
opts: Knowing the hazards of the materials being used
Reading the labels on reagent bottles carefully
Not using laboratory glassware for eating or drinking
Wearing any type of clothes and shoes
items.ans: Wearing any type of clothes and shoes
items.why:
Step 1: check each option.
Knowing hazards, reading labels and not eating from glassware are all good rules.
Step 2: the rules say dress properly: goggles, gloves, shoes and lab coat.
Step 3: so wearing any clothes and shoes is NOT allowed.
That is the answer.
items.clue: Three of these are good habits. Which one breaks a rule about dress?

items.ask: 2. Which laboratory tool is used for approximate measurement of the volume of liquids?
items.why:
Step 1: the question asks about measuring the volume of liquids.
Step 2: of the options, only the measuring cylinder has a volume (ml) scale.
Step 3: a dropper adds drops, a test tube holds liquid, a thermometer measures temperature.
So the book's answer is the measuring cylinder.
Note: in 1.2.1 a beaker gives approximate volume; a cylinder gives a more accurate one.
items.clue: Which tool has a millilitre (ml) scale?

items.ask: 3. Which laboratory equipment is classed as measuring equipment?
items.why:
Step 1: measuring equipment gives you a number.
Step 2: a triple-beam balance gives the mass of an object.
Step 3: a Bunsen burner heats; tongs carry; a stand and clamp hold.
So the answer is the triple-beam balance.
items.clue: Which one gives you a number, like a mass?

items.text: Part I, 1. Natural science is the study of nature and natural laws.
items.why:
Recall 1.1.2.
Natural science studies nature and natural laws.
It includes biology, chemistry and physics.
So the statement is true.
items.clue: Recall the definition of natural science in 1.1.2.

items.text: Part I, 2. Biology, physics and chemistry do not share common areas of study.
items.why:
There is no clear border line between the natural sciences.
Their knowledge overlaps.
Biochemistry and biophysics show this: each joins two sciences.
So they do share areas, and the statement is false.

items.text: Part I, 3. Technology makes life easier or more pleasant and work more productive.
items.why:
Recall 1.1.3.
Technology uses scientific knowledge to help people.
It makes life easier and work more productive.
So the statement is true.
items.clue: Recall what technology is for, from 1.1.3.

items.ask: Part II, 1. The study of living things is the concern of:
items.why:
Bio- means life.
Biology is the study of living things.
Chemistry studies substances, physics matter and energy, geology the earth.
So the answer is biology.

items.ask: Part II, 2. Which branch of natural science studies the nature of matter, energy and their interaction?
items.why:
Natural science has three branches.
Biology → living things. Chemistry → substances.
Physics → matter, energy and their interaction.
So the answer is physics.
items.clue: Recall the three branches of natural science.

items.ask: Part II, 3. Which famous Ethiopian scientist discovered a natural treatment for schistosomiasis (bilharzia)?
items.why:
Dr. Aklilu Lemma found a natural treatment for bilharzia in 1964.
He used endod berries, which kill the snails that spread the disease.
Dr. Gebisa Ejeta worked on sorghum; Prof. Yalemtsehay Mekonnen on physiology and medicinal plants.
So the answer is Dr. Aklilu Lemma.

items.ask: Part II, 4. Which of these is NOT a laboratory safety rule?
opts: Light the match before you turn on the gas of a Bunsen burner
You should add water to acid
You should tie back loose hair
Do not suck solution into a pipette by mouth
items.ans: You should add water to acid
items.why:
Step 1: the question asks which is NOT a safety rule.
Step 2: the rule is "AW! Not WA!": add acid to water.
Step 3: so "You should add water to acid" is wrong.
The other three are real safety rules.
So the answer is "You should add water to acid".

items.ask: Part II, 5. Which is a branch of knowledge and the systematic study of the universe, based on facts, observation and experiments?
items.why:
Recall 1.1.1.
Science is the systematic study of the world.
It is based on facts, observation and experiments.
A theory is only one part of science; dogma is belief that is never tested.
So the answer is science.

items.ask: Part III, 1. Biochemistry is a combination of:
items.why:
Split the word: bio + chemistry.
Bio- means life → biology.
The rest is chemistry.
So biochemistry = biology and chemistry.
items.clue: Split the word into two parts.

items.ask: Part III, 2. Physical chemistry is a combination of:
items.why:
Read each word in the name.
Physical → physics.
Chemistry → chemistry.
So physical chemistry = chemistry and physics.
items.clue: Read each word in the name.

items.ask: Part III, 3. Biophysics is a combination of:
items.why:
Split the word: bio + physics.
Bio- means life → biology.
The rest is physics.
So biophysics = biology and physics.
items.clue: Split the word into two parts.

items.ask: Part III, 4. Geophysics is a combination of:
items.why:
Split the word: geo + physics.
Geo- means earth → geology.
The rest is physics.
So geophysics = geology and physics.

test.text: Put these parts of a laboratory report in order.
test.why:
Step 1: Title first: what the experiment is.
Step 2: Objective: what you want to find out.
Step 3: Procedure: the steps you followed.
Step 4: Observation: what you saw and measured.
Step 5: Conclusion: a short answer to the objective.

test.ask: Purpose of a report: a laboratory report explains what you did, what you learnt and what the ___ mean.
test.why:
A report tells three things.
What you did, and what you learnt.
And what the results of the experiment mean.
So the missing word is results.

test.text: Parts of a report: in which part do you list the steps you followed?
test.why:
The procedure is the steps you followed, in order.
The title names the experiment; the date says when.
The conclusion answers the objective.
So the answer is procedure.
